title: Five single-indicator fits raise held-night error for 32 GJ 191 HARPS exposures from 2021
abstract: We test whether line-shape measurements explain rapid differences between DRS and SERVAL velocities of GJ 191. Eight selected nights in HARPS-RVBank version 02 have 32 exposures. We remove a separate offset and time slope from each night. A common indicator slope fitted on seven nights predicts the residuals of the excluded night. All five single-indicator fits raise weighted error. The primary bisector fit raises error by 10.9 percent. Width, contrast, chromatic index and differential line width raise error by 7.5, 5.8, 14.5 and 1.8 percent. This is a test of a common linear response in the same selected spectra. Small samples, shared errors and nonlinear responses limit the result. The cause remains open. No planet or independent instrument confirmation is reported. The package contains original code, aggregate evidence, a figure, input provenance and separate-scratch retrieval steps.
